sections.h2: Is a listing, a private sale or a cash sale best in Mamaroneck, NY?
sections.html:
Any of the three can work for a Mamaroneck house. The town's median owner-occupied home value is above $1 million, so a sale is a major financial decision, and some owners prefer a buyer who skips the repair list.

  • Listing: draws the most buyers, along with showings, inspection haggling and a financing contingency.
  • Private sale: you screen buyers yourself and lean on your attorney for the paperwork.
  • Cash sale: staging, fixes and open houses drop out when the buyer takes the house as it is.

One local step comes before any of these. Confirm whether your address is in the unincorporated Town, the Village of Mamaroneck or the Village of Larchmont, because the building and tax offices you deal with depend on it.

sections.h2: How is the Town of Mamaroneck laid out?
sections.html:
The Town of Mamaroneck covers 14.07 square miles in Westchester County, and 7.41 of those square miles are water, which is 52.85% of the total. Its land area is 6.65 square miles. The town contains two villages, Larchmont and the Village of Mamaroneck, though part of the Village of Mamaroneck lies in the neighboring Town of Rye. Most of the town's land is unincorporated, yet most residents live inside the villages.

Much of the unincorporated area receives mail through the Larchmont Post Office, so a Larchmont mailing address does not tell you which municipality governs the lot. The Town Center is at 740 West Boston Post Road.

The town's history shows up in sale listings and buyer questions. An Englishman named John Richbell bought the land from the Siwanoy in 1661, and the State Legislature created the town on March 7, 1788. The Mamaroneck River marks the boundary with the Town of Rye. The villages formed in the 1890s because a town could then run only elections, courts and highways, so Larchmont Manor and the harbor area incorporated to get water, sewers, sidewalks, lighting and police. Larchmont Manor had become a summer resort for New York City families, and in the early 1920s the area had a silent-film studio. Winged Foot Golf Club, which opened in 1923, hosted the U.S. Open most recently in 2020. Population grew from 29,156 in 2010 to 31,758 in 2020.

sections.h2: How expensive and how settled is the Mamaroneck housing market?
sections.html:
The middle home among owners in the Town of Mamaroneck is valued at $1,076,700, and households earn a middle figure of $163,781. Two of every three homes (66.9%) are lived in by owners. The rest of the figures here come from the Census Bureau's profile of the town.

The town has 11,684 households averaging 2.64 people, and 70.5% of residents past age 25 have finished a bachelor's degree. With the midpoint above $1 million, a good share of sales here will land where the state's 1% mansion tax begins, and the buyer pays that one.

sections.h2: What is the Mamaroneck calendar for contesting an assessment?
sections.html:
Grievances run from June 1 to the third Tuesday of June, and the 2026 window has closed. The town's key dates page sets the yearly calendar, so the next one opens June 1, 2027 and ends June 15, 2027, when the Board of Assessment Review sits.

  • May 1: taxable status date, the day ownership and condition are measured and the deadline for exemption applications.
  • June 1: the tentative roll goes online and in the office, and change-of-assessment notices are mailed to all owners, even those with no change.
  • Third Tuesday in June: the office must have every grievance in hand by then, delivered or mailed. A postmark does not rescue a late one, and email does not work.
  • September 15: the final roll appears and filing opens for Small Claims Assessment Review petitions.

The valuation date is July 1 of the prior year, so the 2026 roll reflects what a property was worth in mid-2025. The town assessor page adds that the office reviews every property transfer for accuracy, using the RP-5217 form signed at closing, and corrects the sale information it records.

sections.h2: Which Mamaroneck building and flood rules should a seller check?
sections.html:
The Town's Building and Code Enforcement department now takes permit applications online through the OpenGov Viewpoint portal, and first-time users must create an account. The department page says it issues permits for new construction, additions, alterations, plumbing, signs, erosion control and tree removal. Many jobs need a second approval from Engineering for erosion and sediment control, the Highway Department for work in the road, or the Environmental Planner for trees.

New York adopted the 2025 building standards, and work covered by the state codes after December 31, 2025 must meet them. The Town also adopted the 2020 NYStretch Energy Code and the 2025 Energy Conservation Construction Code, applying whichever provision is stricter for each component.

With more than half the town's area under water and a recorded elevation of zero feet, flood maps matter here. The department page links to the FEMA Flood Map Service Center and to FEMA's guidance on changing a flood zone. Check your parcel on the map before listing, and keep any elevation certificate nearby.

One warning from the same page applies to anyone dealing with zoning or planning matters: applicants have been the target of repeated phishing emails. The Town says it would never send correspondence from a board chairman or ask for money by wire transfer, so treat any message that does as fraudulent and call the department using the number on the Town's own site.

sections.h2: How much does Westchester County charge to transfer a Mamaroneck deed?
sections.html:
The Westchester County Clerk's fee page applies the state's $2 per $500 and shows a $404,501 purchase owing $1,620. Carried to the town's $1,076,700 midpoint, the state tax comes to roughly $4,308, and a buyer at that price would add about $10,767 in mansion tax.

A residential deed carries a $45 recording fee, $5 a page, a $5 TP-584 filing and a $125 RP-5217 filing. For a three-page deed in a single municipality the clerk shows a $190 total. The office asks filers to calculate exact amounts in its Property Records Electronic Portal, and taxes can be paid by ACH, cash, check or money order.

Once the sale closes, end your STAR registration as the state's STAR page instructs, and let the buyer register for their own credit.

faqs.q: Is Mamaroneck a town or a village?
faqs.a: Both exist. The Town of Mamaroneck contains the Village of Larchmont, part of the Village of Mamaroneck and a large unincorporated area. Check which one governs your address before contacting a building or tax office.

faqs.q: When must a Mamaroneck grievance be filed?
faqs.a: By the third Tuesday of June. The 2026 window has closed, and the next one runs from June 1 to June 15, 2027. The office takes grievances in person or by mail, never by email.

faqs.q: Which dates set a Mamaroneck assessment?
faqs.a: Assessments reflect property condition and ownership on May 1, and values are based on market value on July 1 of the prior year. The 2026 roll uses mid-2025 values.

faqs.q: Does Mamaroneck require a permit for home work?
faqs.a: Yes for new construction, additions, alterations and plumbing, and the department invites owners to call if unsure. Filing happens in the online permit portal, and some projects also need engineering, highway or tree approvals.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer taxes on a Mamaroneck sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays the state's $2 per $500 unless the contract moves it. The buyer pays the 1% mansion tax once a residential price reaches $1 million, a figure the town's midpoint home value already exceeds.
